title: Integrated Gaussian crossing limit
statement: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\gamma$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$, as $\theta\to0$ through positive values, $\int \frac{|\Phi((t-\sin\theta\,y)/\cos\theta)-\Phi(t)|}{\theta}\,d\gamma(y)$ tends to $\varphi(t)\int |y|\,d\gamma(y)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ denote the standard Gaussian distribution function and density. For $t,y\in\mathbb R$, define $q_{t,y}(\theta)=\Phi((t-\sin\theta\,y)/\cos\theta)-\Phi(t)$. For every real $t$, if $Y\sim N(0,1)$, then $\mathbb E_Y(|q_{t,Y}(\theta)|/\theta)\to\varphi(t)\mathbb E|Y|$ as $\theta\to0^+$.
